targetAudience.primary: Multi-agent runtime, reliability and debugging engineers
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands agent execution traces, root-cause analysis and basic evaluation metrics.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Multi-agent incident tooling often forces one root-cause label even when several causal explanations remain plausible and actionable.

whyNow: MP-Bench turns multi-perspective failure attribution into a concrete expert-annotated benchmark and exposes large disagreement among screened annotators, making causal ambiguity measurable rather than anecdotal.

externalHook.description: A failed execution can have one immutable trace but several reasonable causal explanations; forcing one label may discard useful diagnostic evidence.

coreProposition: Failure attribution should be represented as a ranked diagnostic evidence set, not a single root-cause label.

originalValue.description: Derives a four-layer runtime model separating immutable trace facts, plural failure hypotheses, consensus/salience, and a singular governed repair decision.

readerTakeaway: Preserve causal ambiguity without blocking action: store hypotheses append-only with provenance, rank them without confusing consensus with independent proof, and let one bounded repair decision cite several still-plausible causes.

supported: MP-Bench contains 289 failed logs from 121 MAS configurations and uses three independent expert annotators per instance.
The paper reports that only 16.2% of failure-labeled steps are identified by all three annotators, while 56.1% are identified by only one.
The benchmark ranks failure steps by annotator consensus and evaluates predicted rankings with nDCG rather than a single oracle label.
The paper reports benefits from non-deterministic sampling and tested cross-model combinations within its evaluation protocol.
unsupported: That every real MAS failure has multiple equally valid causes
That multi-LLM attribution is universally superior in production
Independent reproduction of the complete MP-Bench results
uncertain: How to calibrate causal confidence across correlated diagnostic agents
When a hypothesis should become operationally decisive
How the approach transfers to software engineering and enterprise incidents

firstPartyRole.rationale: The conclusion is a general multi-agent reliability architecture and does not require a first-party project mapping.

decisionReason: The paper supplies concrete expert disagreement, benchmark construction and evaluation mechanisms; the Research Center adds a bounded diagnostic evidence model that is useful beyond source summary.
